schema: §2.7 (v0.50) -- complete per-sentence segment disposition, superseding §21 R6's not_annotatable-only shape. `not_annotatable` (R6's original array, the only key run_scoring.load_not_annotatable() reads) is preserved for scoring and holds every NOT_OBLIGATION_BEARING / NOT_ANNOTATABLE / EXCLUDED span. `dispositions` is the full per-sentence record §2.7 requires, covering ANNOTATED and AMBIGUOUS spans too, which `not_annotatable` deliberately excludes -- an AMBIGUOUS span is an open reviewer question, not a settled non-item, and including it in the scoring array would resolve it silently.

reconciliation.note: Both sentences are obligation-bearing and both are annotated; nothing is left undisposed. observations.label: A THIRD _WITHIN_RE reachability gap -- the UNIT alternation -- RULED NOT TO BE A TAG
observations.status: RECORDED, NOT TAGGED. Reviewer ruling 2026-09-24 (guideline v0.65, §8.13). Queued as §10.1 F23.
observations.note:
THE SECOND OF TWO REACHABILITY GAPS IN E02-02's TEMPORAL, RULED NOT TO BE A TAG (v0.65, section 8.13; queued as section 10.1 F23). Recorded here rather than resolved inside an annotation pass, the same way C04-051#temporal-composition and C04-072#temporal-composition were logged before F21 ruled them.

THE MECHANISM, VERIFIED BY EXECUTION AND MECHANISTICALLY DISTINCT FROM THE NUMERAL GAP. ir_compile._UNIT_ALTERNATION is 'business\s+days?|days?|hours?|weeks?|months?|years?|bd|h|d|w|mo|y' and has no entry for 'calendar days'. That is a DIFFERENT sub-pattern of _WITHIN_RE from the numeral group the section 8.13 tag records, and it has a different fix -- a one-word alternation widening ('(?:calendar|continuous|consecutive)\s+'?) against genuine numeral parsing. Each gap alone rejects this phrase: 'within 3 calendar days of receipt' -> None with the numeral already bare, and 'within three (3) days of receipt' -> None with the unit already accepted.

WHY IT IS NOT MINTED AS A TAG, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. Swept over every WITHIN deadline in a modal sentence across all 28 documents -- 179 in total, with the sweep gated on six named known answers AND on reconciling exactly with corpus.py's own published bare/parenthetical split (20/159) before any count was read off it:
  accepted (compiles)        8   4.5%   4 docs
  numeral only              48  26.8%  20 docs
  numeral + preposition    103  57.5%  21 docs
  preposition only          12   6.7%   8 docs
  numeral + unit             2   1.1%   2 docs
  numeral + unit + prep      6   3.4%   4 docs
THE UNIT GAP HAS EIGHT INSTANCES ACROSS 6 DOCUMENTS ('calendar days' x7, 'continuous months' x1) AND ZERO OF THEM OCCUR WITHOUT THE NUMERAL GAP. There is no 'unit' or 'unit+prep' cell at all. So a separate tag could never fire alone on any evidence that exists, and repairing the unit alternation alone would fix ZERO phrases in this corpus. Section 22.1's discipline applies directly: a kind is not ruled on a sample of one, and E02-02 would be that sample.

FORCING FUNCTION, stated precisely so the next session does not have to re-derive it: a SECOND independent instance, or -- far more informative -- an instance where the unit gap occurs WITHOUT the numeral gap, which has never happened in 179 deadlines and is the only evidence that would give a separate tag discriminating power.

A MEASUREMENT DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY AND REPORTED, NOT FIXED. corpus.py's published `within_parenthetical` statistic SILENTLY ABSORBS this class: classify_within() reconstructs a probe 'within {blob} {unit} of X' and buckets any rejection as parenthetical, so all 8 unit instances are counted as numeral ones. The inflation is 8 of 159 (5.0%), and section 11's still-open scope decision on widening _WITHIN_RE is made against that number. This is exactly the objection section 8.6 itself raised against folding its preposition gap into section 8's parenthetical row: 'filing them together would inflate the parenthetical gap's measured size with cases that are trivially fixable'.

SEARCH KEY: within_parenthetical, calendar days, _UNIT_ALTERNATION, _WITHIN_RE, unit modifier, F23, E02-006, E02-02. Preserved screen: evals/goldens/holdout/within_parenthetical/screen.py.
